%BQUOTE.help: Mask special characters and mnemonic operators in a resolved value at macro execution.

%DEQUOTE.help:
Removes matching quotation marks from a character string that begins with a quotation mark, 
and deletes all characters to the right of the closing quotation mark.

%NRBQUOTE.help: Masks special characters, including & and %, and mnemonic operators in a resolved value at macro execution.

%EVAL.help: Evaluates arithmetic and logical expressions using integer arithmetic.

%INDEX.help: Returns the position of the first character of a string.

%LENGTH.help: Returns the length of a string.

%QUOTE.help: Mask special characters and mnemonic operators in a resolved value at macro execution.

%NRQUOTE.help: Masks special characters, including & and %, and mnemonic operators in a resolved value at macro execution.

%SCAN.help: Searches for a word that is specified by its position in a string.

%QSCAN.help: Searches for a word and masks special characters and mnemonic operators.

%STR.help: Mask special characters and mnemonic operators in constant text at macro compilation.

%NRSTR.help: Masks special characters, including & and %, and mnemonic operators in constant text during macro compilation.

%SUBSTR.help: Produce a substring of a character string.

%QSUBSTR.help: Produces a substring and masks special characters and mnemonic operators.

%SUPERQ.help: Masks all special characters and mnemonic operators at macro execution but prevents further resolution of the value.

%SYMEXIST.help: Returns an indication of the existence of a macro variable.

%SYMGLOBL.help: Returns an indication as to whether a macro variable is global in scope.

%SYMLOCAL.help: Returns an indication as to whether a macro variable is local in scope.

%SYSEVALF.help: Evaluates arithmetic and logical expressions using floating-point arithmetic.

%SYSFUNC.help: Execute SAS functions or user-written functions.

%QSYSFUNC.help: Executes functions and masks special characters and mnemonic operators.

%SYSGET.help: Returns the character string that is the value of the environment variable passed as the argument.

%SYSPROD.help: Reports whether a SAS software product is licensed at the site.

%UNQUOTE.help: During macro execution, unmasks all special characters and mnemonic operators for a value.

%LOWCASE.help:
[Syntax: %LOWCASE (character string | text expression)]

Converts characters to lowercase. LOWCASE returns a result without quotation marks, even if the 
argument has quotation marks.

%QLOWCASE.help:
Syntax: %QLOWCASE(text | text expression)

Changes uppercase characters to lowercase and returns a result that masks special 
characters and mnemonic operators.

%QUPCASE.help: Converts a value to uppercase and returns a result that masks special characters and mnemonic operators.

%PUT.help: Returns a value using a specified format.

%TPLOT.help:
The %TPLOT macro creates a triangular plot that graphically displays genetic marker 
test results. The plot has colors and shapes representing p-value ranges for tests 
of the following quantities: linkage disequilibrium between pairs of markers, Hardy-
Weinberg equilibrium (HWE) for individual markers, and associations between markers 
and a dichotomous trait (such as disease status).

%SYSMACEXEC.help: Returns an indication of the execution status of a macro.

%SYSMACEXIST.help: Returns an indication of the existence of a macro definition in the Work.SASMacr or Work.SASMacn catalog.

%SYSMEXECDEPTH.help: Returns the nesting depth of macro execution from the point of the call to %SYSMEXECDEPTH.

%SYSMEXECNAME.help: Returns the name of the macro executing at a requested nesting level.

%CMPRES.help:
Syntax: %CMPRES (text | text expression)

Compresses multiple blanks and removes leading and trailing blanks.

%QCMPRES.help:
Syntax: %QCMPRES (text | text expression)

Compresses multiple blanks and removes leading and trailing blanks.

%QCMPRES masks the result so special characters and mnemonic operators are treated 
as text instead of being interpreted by the macro facility.

%COMPSTOR.help:
Syntax: %COMPSTOR (PATHNAME=SAS-data-library)

Compiles macros and stores them in a catalog in a permanent SAS library.

%DATATYP.help:
Syntax:%DATATYP (text | text expression)

Returns the data type (numeric or char) of a value.

%LEFT.help:
Syntax: %LEFT(text | text expression)
    
Left-aligns an argument by removing leading blanks.

%QLEFT.help:
Syntax: %QLEFT(text | text expression)

Left-aligns an argument by removing leading blanks.

QLEFT masks the result so special characters and mnemonic operators are treated as 
text instead of being interpreted by the macro facility.

%SYSRC.help:
[Syntax: %SYSRC(character-string)]

Returns a value corresponding to an error condition.

%TRIM.help:
Syntax: %TRIM(text | text expression)

Trim trailing blanks.

%QTRIM.help:
Syntax: %QTRIM(text | text expression)
    
Trim trailing blanks. Masks special characters and mnemonic operators.

%VERIFY.help:
Syntax: %VERIFY(source, excerpt)
    
Returns the position of the first character unique to an expression.

%DQLOAD.help:
Syntax: %DQLOAD(DQLOCALE=(locale1 ...localeN), DQSETUPLOC=`file-specification', <DQINFO=0 | 1>)
    
Sets system option values and loads locales into memory.

%DQPUTLOC.help:
Syntax: %DQPUTLOC(locale, <SHORT=0 | 1>, <PARSEDEFN=0 | 1)>
    
Displays current information on a specified locale in the SAS log.

%DQUNLOAD.help:
Syntax: %DQUNLOAD 
    
Unloads all locales to increase the amount of free memory.

%KLOWCASE.help:
Syntax: %KLOWCASE (text | text expression) 

Changes uppercase alphabetic characters to their lowercase equivalents. If the argument 
might contain a special character or mnemonic operator, listed below, use %QKLOWCAS. 

%KLOWCASE returns a result without quotation marks, even if the argument has quotation marks. 
%QKLOWCAS produces a result with the following special characters and mnemonic operators masked 
so the macro processor interprets them as text instead of as elements of the macro language: 

  & % ' " ( ) + - * / < > = ¬ ^ ~ ; , blank AND OR NOT EQ NE LE LT GE GT IN 

Autocall macros are included in a SAS library. This library might not be installed at your site 
or might be a site-specific version. If you cannot access this macro or if you want to find out 
if the library is a site-specific version, see your on-site SAS support personnel.

%KVERIFY.help:
Syntax: %KVERIFY (source, excerpt) 

Returns the position of the first character unique to an expression. 

Arguments:
source 
  is text or a text expression that you want to examine for characters that do not exist in excerpt. 
excerpt 
  is text or a text expression that defines the set of characters that %KVERIFY uses to examine source.

%ARMEND.help:
Indicates the termination of an application. 
    
Syntax: %ARMEND< (option-1 <, ...option-n>)>; 

Available options are:

  APPID=numeric variable or constant 
  is the application ID to use on the ARM_GETID function call. The value must be a numeric 
  variable or constant. 

  APPIDVAR=numeric variable 
  is the application ID. The value must be a numeric variable.

  LEVEL=numeric variable or constant 
  is a variable that specifies the execution level. The value must be a numeric constant or variable.

  MACONLY=NO | YES 
  enables the %ARMEND macro to be issued in open code. You set the value to YES if the macro can be 
  issued in open code, and NO if it can be issued only in a DATA step.

  Default: NO 

  SCL=NO | YES 
  is used only in SCL programs and specifies whether the macro is in an SCL environment. Set the value
  to YES if the macro is in an SCL environment, and NO if it is not. Default: NO

%ARMGTID.help:
Assigns a unique identifier to a transaction class. 
    
Syntax: %ARMGTID (TXNNAME='transaction-name' < option-1 <, ...option-n>>); 

Use the %ARMGTID macro to name a transaction class. Transaction classes are related 
units of work within an application. One or more %ARMGTID macros are typically issued 
when the application starts to name each of the transaction classes used by the application. 
The %ARMGTID macro produces only one 
record for each transaction class, even if there are multiple %ARMGTID macros for the 
same transaction class.

%ARMINIT.help:
Signifies the initialization of an application. 
    
Syntax: %ARMINIT (APPNAME='application-name' <, option-1 <, ...option-n>>); 

Available options are:

  APPIDVAR=numeric variable -- is the application ID. The value must be a numeric variable. 

  APPUSER='application-userID' -- is the application user ID. The value is a SAS character variable or quoted literal. 

  GETID=NO | YES -- is optional and denotes whether to generate an ARM_GETID function call after ARM_INIT. Default: NO 

  LEVEL=numeric constant or variable -- is a variable that specifies the execution level. 

  MACONLY=NO | YES -- enables the %ARMINIT macro to be issued in open code. Default: NO 

  SCL=NO | YES -- is used only in SCL programs and specifies whether the macro is in an SCL environment. Default: NO 

  TXNIDVAR=numeric variable -- is a numeric variable that contains the value of the transaction ID. 

  TXNDET='name' -- is a transaction detail. The value is a SAS character variable or quoted literal. 

  TXNNAME='transaction-name' -- is the transaction name. The value is a SAS character variable or quoted literal value.

%ARMSTOP.help:
Marks the end of a transaction instance. 
    
Syntax: %ARMSTOP (<option1 <, ...option-n>>);

Available options are:

  LEVEL=numeric constant or variable 
  is a variable that specifies the execution level. The value must be a numeric constant or variable.

  MACONLY=NO | YES 
  enables the %ARMSTOP macro to be issued in open code. You set the value to YES if the macro can be 
  issued in open code, and NO if it can be issued only in a DATA step. 

  METRVAL1-7='name' 
  is the value of the user-defined metric. The value must be a SAS character variable or a quoted literal 
  value up to eight characters in length.

  SCL=NO | YES 
  is used only in SCL programs and specifies whether the macro is in an SCL environment. Set the value 
  to YES if the macro is in an SCL environment, and NO if it is not. Default: NO 

  SHANDLE=numeric variable or constant 
  is the start handle to use on the ARM_UPDATE function call. The value must be a numeric variable or constant. 

  SHDLVAR=numeric variable 
  is a numeric variable that contains the value of the start handle. 

  STATUS=numeric variable or numeric constant 
  is a transaction status value to pass to the ARM_STOP function call. The value must be a numeric 
  variable or numeric constant 0, 1, or 2. The default is 0.

%ARMSTRT.help:
Signals the start of execution of a transaction instance and returns a unique handle that is passed 
to %ARMUPDT and %ARMSTOP. 

Syntax: %ARMSTRT (option-1 <, ...option-n>); 

Available options are: 

  APPID=numeric variable or constant -- is the application ID to use on the ARM_GETID function call. 

  APPIDVAR=numeric variable -- is the application ID. The value must be a numeric variable.

  CORR=n -- defines the type of parent and child transactions. Default: 0 

  GETID=NO | YES -- is optional and denotes whether to generate an ARM_GETID function call before ARM_START. Default: NO 

  LEVEL=numeric constant or variable 
  is a variable that specifies the execution level. The value must be a numeric constant or variable.

  MACONLY=NO | YES -- enables the %ARMSTRT macro to be issued in open code. Default: NO 

  METRVAL1-7='name' -- is the value of the user-defined metric. The value must be a SAS character variable or a quoted literal.  

  PARNTVAR=numeric variable -- is a numeric variable that contains the value of the parent transaction start handle. 

  SCL=NO | YES -- is used only in SCL programs and specifies whether the macro is in an SCL environment. Default: NO 

  SHDLVAR=numeric variable -- is a numeric variable that contains the value of the start handle. 

  TXNDET='name' -- is a transaction detail. The value is a SAS character variable or quoted literal.

  TXNID=numeric variable or constant -- is the transaction ID to use in the ARM_START function call. 

  TXNIDVAR=numeric variable -- is a numeric variable that contains the value of the transaction ID when GETID=NO. . 

  TXNNAME='transaction-name' -- is the transaction name. The value is a SAS character variable or quoted literal.

%ARMUPDT.help:
Updates a transaction that has been previously started. 
    
Syntax: %ARMUPDT (DATA='variable', <option-1 <, ...option-n>>); 

where: 

  DATA='variable' -- is a SAS character variable or a quoted literal from the user-supplied data buffer that 
  contains text to pass to the ARM_UPDATE function call. DATA= is not required, but it is highly recommended. 

  LEVEL=numeric constant or variable 
  is a variable that specifies the execution level. The value must be a numeric constant or variable.

  MACONLY=NO | YES -- enables the %ARMUPDT macro to be issued in open code. Default: NO 

  METRVAL1-7='name' 
  is the value of the user-defined metric. The value must be a SAS character variable or a quoted literal. 

  SCL=NO | YES 
  is used only in SCL programs and specifies whether the macro is in an SCL environment. Default: NO 

  SHANDLE=numeric or constant 
  is the start handle to use on the ARM_UPDATE function call. The value must be a numeric or constant.

  SHDLVAR=numeric variable -- is a numeric variable that contains the value of the start handle.

%ARMCONV.help:
Converts a SAS System 9 or later ARM log written in simple format to the more readable 
label=item ARM format used in Release 8.2.

%ARMJOIN.help:
Reads the six SAS data sets created by the %ARMPROC macro and creates SAS data sets and 
SQL views that contain common information about applications and transactions.

Syntax: %ARMJOIN (<option-1 <, ...option-n>>); 

Available options are: 

  LIBIN=libref 
  is the libref for the SAS library that contains the six SAS data sets that are created 
  by the %ARMPROC macro. Default: WORK 

  LIBOUT=libref 
  is the libref for the SAS library that contains the application and transaction data sets. 
  Default: WORK 
  Restriction: If a Read-only library is specified in the LIBOUT= option, an error message 
  is written to the ARM log and processing is stopped. 

  TXNDS=YES | NO 
  specifies whether the transaction data sets are to be created. Default: YES 

  UPDTDS=YES | NO 
  specifies whether the update data sets are to be created. Default: YES

%ARMPROC.help:
Processes an input ARM log and outputs six SAS data sets that contain the gathered 
information from the log. 
    
Syntax: %ARMPROC (<option-1 <, ...option-n>>); 

Available options are:

  LIB=libref 
  is the libref for the SAS library that contains the six SAS data sets. Default: WORK 

  LOG=pathname 
  is the pathname for the physical location of the ARM log. If a pathname is not specified, 
  you must pre-assign the ARMLOG fileref before calling the macro.

  LOGNEW=pathname 
  is the pathname of the physical location of the new ARM log. It is used when ARM 
  processing is resumed.

%PERFEND.help:
Syntax: %PERFEND;
    
Indicates the termination of the application.

Use the %PERFEND macro to terminate an application or user event. Each %PERFEND macro 
is paired with one %PERFINIT macro to mark the end of an application. The %PERFEND means 
that the application does not issue any more ARM calls. ARM calls issued after an application 
has been terminated with the %PERFEND macro result in an error. All transaction class 
identifiers are cleared and are no longer available after the %PERFEND macro.

%PERFSTOP.help:
Specifies the end of a transaction. 
    
Syntax: %PERFSTOP; 

There are no input parameters for the %PERFSTOP macro. 

Use the %PERFSTOP macro to signal the end of a transaction that was started using 
the %PERFSTRT macro. The %PERFSTOP macro contains default user metrics. To see the 
relationships between %PERFSTOP and the default user metrics, see Default User 
Metrics and Performance Macros.
